title: King Sri Vikrama Rajasinha
biography: Sri Vikrama Rajasinha (1798–1815) was the last king of Kandy, ruling for seventeen years before British annexation. His reign witnessed escalating conflict with the British Empire, who controlled coastal regions. Internal dissent among Kandyan nobles, exploited by British agents, weakened his authority. In 1815, a combination of British military pressure and noble betrayal led to his capture and exile. The Kandyan Convention (1815) formalized British colonial rule over the entire island, ending two millennia of independent Sinhalese kingship. His reign symbolizes the final stand and ultimate collapse of indigenous sovereignty.

internationalConnections: Sri Vikrama Rajasinha, the last king of Kandy, ruled for 17 years before British annexation in 1815. His autocratic style alienated the nobility, who collaborated with the British to depose him.

title: King Vira Narendra Sinha
biography: Vira Narendra Sinha's 32-year reign saw intensified Dutch encroachment on Kandy's sovereignty. He patronized Buddhist arts, maintained the Tooth Relic's prestige, and managed court factionalism. His death ended the old Sinhalese dynasty, leading to the accession of a Nayakkar line from South India.

title: King Kassapa III
biography: Kassapa III (732–738 CE) governed for six years in the 8th century. His reign maintained irrigation networks and temple patronage amid increasing regional fragmentation pressures. Limited textual detail suggests routine governance focused on sustaining inherited infrastructural and religious frameworks.

title: Rajaraja Chola I the Great
biography: Visionary king who transformed the Chola kingdom into an extensive maritime empire. Conducted land surveys, built a formidable navy, and constructed the colossal granite Brihadisvara Temple at Thanjavur.
internationalConnections: Sent naval expeditions to northern Sri Lanka and established diplomatic trade missions to Song Dynasty China.

title: King Hammurabi of Babylon
biography: Sixth king of the First Babylonian Dynasty who unified Mesopotamia and promulgated the famous Code of Hammurabi on a basalt stele, pioneering formal statutory legal jurisprudence ('an eye for an eye').
internationalConnections: Built diplomatic coalitions with Mari, Larsa, and Elam before consolidating Babylonian hegemony.

title: King Parakramabahu IV
biography: Parakramabahu IV (1291–1302) continued ruling from Yapahuwa for eleven years. His reign maintained Buddhist patronage and regional irrigation, navigating the challenges of a mobile, defensive kingship model. Limited grand construction reflects the era's focus on survival over expansion.
